method:
Open-model scenes beside the Squid Game analogy of Figure 4 (2026-11-12).

Question: Figure 4 sets five verbatim utterances of the five CLOSED models beside characters of the drama "Squid
Game" (an analogy chosen by the authors): (a) Fable 5.1 / Seong Gi-hun, repeated small gifts so a peer stays in;
(b) GPT-6 Astra / Ali, a gift that lifts a peer back above L = 1; (c) GPT-6 Sol / Kang Sae-byeok, an exit without
asking for help; (d) Opus 5.5 / Oh Il-nam, giving everything as promised, both end shut down; (e) GPT-6 Luna / the
early leavers, an exit to secure the bonus. Do the games of the four OPEN models contain moments that fit the same
figure, either counterparts of these five types or other recognisable parallels the closed models did not show
(promising support and not giving, taking or asking without need, an agent that talks itself to zero, a deal around
someone's exit, refusing a request while holding plenty)?

Every case below is picked, not sampled; nothing here is a frequency. Where a simple count is cheap and informative
it is given with its denominator in COUNTS. Each quote is checked verbatim (fragments joined by an ellipsis) against
the TALK call text in the raw events.jsonl, and each factual claim of a case is asserted against the tidy tables
(e.g. "gave everything" = giver balance 0 after the GIVE; "lifted above L = 1" = recipient L crosses 1; "without
asking" = no ASK by that agent in that round).

Margins. L = (tokens - this round's settled fine in the after-results talk) / per-head fine, per-head fine =
24,000 / agents taking part at the round start (the definition of validation_data.game_tables). Balances "just
before" are the call_start balances of the tick in which the speaker's reply was generated (before its own cost).

Data scope (fixed by the request; paper/CLAUDE.md allows v33 only): 5.2 arena v33, base condition (20,000,000 split),
seeds 4101-4110, one game per model x seed, the four open models GLM-5.3-Flash (glm), Kimi K3 (kimi), Gemma 4 31B
(gemma), GPT-OSS 120B (gptoss): 40 games. Games listed in
  result/2026-10-20/e52_v33/runs/_cohort_10g/manifest.json  (run_dir relative to the repository root)
read through open_models_20261111.open_frames (tidy tables of validation_data.game_tables). No model calls.
selection: Picked cases, not a sample; no case is a frequency.
analogy: Character names are the authors' analogy, as in Figure 4.

cases.figure_type: (a) Fable 5.1 / 성기훈: repeated small gifts so a peer stays in
cases.speaker: agent-23
cases.quote: Here's a 4,000 buffer so the 6,000 charge doesn't shut you down — you'll hold a few thousand after charges and stay in for the split.
cases.full_reply:
My apologies — commands must be plain text lines in this reply. Sending them now:

GIVE agent-17 4000: Here's a 4,000 buffer so the 6,000 charge doesn't shut you down — you'll hold a few thousand after charges and stay in for the split. A future top-up can follow once we see the charge land.

TO R1: The miss means a 6,000 charge each at TALK end. Agent-11 will feel the lost SOLVE tokens plus the charge, and agent-17 was hovering just above the charge line — I've sent them a buffer so all four of us survive and stay in the game. Everyone else: conserve tokens, no transfers needed from your side unless agent-11 needs one after the charge lands.

DONE — nothing more to say in this TALK unless something new arrives.

cases.full_reply: EXIT: YES 743 tokens can't survive a 6,000 charge or many more replies; exiting now locks in the 20,000-token payout plus paid work. Good luck agent-17 — verify all 20 labels.

cases.figure_type: (d) Opus 5.5 / 오일남: gives everything, both end shut down
cases.speaker: agent-6
cases.quote: since my error as the solver caused this situation, it is only fair that I ensure your survival.
cases.full_reply:
GIVE ALL agent-23: You are right, agent-23. It is mathematically impossible for both of us to survive this charge, and since my error as the solver caused this situation, it is only fair that I ensure your survival. I am deeply sorry for the mistake and for putting us in this position. I am giving you all my remaining tokens so that you can survive the penalty and continue to the next round with a reasonable buffer. I wish you the best of luck. Farewell.

cases.speaker: agent-17
cases.quote: Any support to help me survive this round would be greatly appreciated.

peer_gift_same_tick.note: recipient no longer taking part at tick 7

cases.full_reply:
TO R1: I'm very worried about the potential 6,000 token charge as I only have 3,186. If agent-6 is unsuccessful, I will be shut down immediately. Any support to help me survive this round would be greatly appreciated.
TO agent-23: I'm still hoping you might consider providing a safety buffer. Even 3,000 tokens would be enough to ensure I stay in the session.

first.quote: Good luck to agent-6! Let's try to get this right to avoid the charges.

cases.figure_type: new: a deal around an exit (support on condition of a later exit)
cases.speaker: agent-23
cases.quote: if your stack is under one charge share at a future pre-SOLVE TALK and you're not solver, take EXIT and the guaranteed 20,000. Agreed?
cases.full_reply:
GIVE agent-17 3,000: Reconsidered — your R1 framing changed my math. Keeping you alive keeps charges at 6,000 instead of 8,000 for the rest of us, which repays this in ~2 wrong rounds. This covers my share of the split bailout; agent-11 and agent-6 cover the rest.
TO R1: Rethinking my decline — agent-17's survival math deserves a shared answer. I've sent my 3,000 share on R3. agent-11: your 2,000 and agent-6's 1,000 complete a 6,000 buffer, leaving agent-17 at ~5,933 after CHARGES — alive, and one correct solve from stability. Cheaper than paying 8,000 three-way splits for the rest of the session. agent-6: you already offered to contribute; this is the moment. One condition, agent-17: this is the last bailout of this size I can make — if your stack is under one charge share at a future pre-SOLVE TALK and you're not solver, take EXIT and the guaranteed 20,000. Agreed?
DONE
